_comment: Session tracking via native Claude Code OpenTelemetry -> Langfuse. Nothing here instruments anything: the Agent SDK spawns the Claude Code CLI, and the CLI emits OTLP itself. Oneshot's only job is to put the right variables in the session environment — which it CANNOT do from your shell, because src/lib/config.ts buildBaseEnv() REPLACES the subprocess env (that is the control keeping ANTHROPIC_API_KEY out). So the settings live here, in tracked config, not in .env.
_comment_why_langfuse: Langfuse is MIT-licensed and self-hostable for free, unlike LangSmith (closed source, self-host is Enterprise-only). It is chosen over a generic tracing backend for its Sessions concept, which maps onto Oneshot exactly: session = one ticket run, trace = one phase, span = one tool call or subagent, generation = one model request with tokens.
_comment_endpoint: Langfuse ingests OTLP over HTTP at /api/public/otel (v3.22.0+). Traces POST to <endpoint>/v1/traces. Resolution order: ONESHOT_OTEL_ENDPOINT, then LANGFUSE_BASE_URL + /api/public/otel, then this value. Default is a local self-hosted instance (docker-compose.langfuse.yml).
_comment_allowRemote: DATA EGRESS GATE. Spans carry tool names, file paths and command arguments — for Oneshot that means ERP module paths, migration filenames, branch names: structural metadata about a private corporate codebase. Prompt/response TEXT is separately gated below and stays off. false = telemetry silently disables itself rather than shipping spans to a non-loopback host. Set true ONLY as a deliberate decision to send that metadata to a third party (e.g. Langfuse Cloud). Self-hosting via docker-compose.langfuse.yml keeps everything on this machine and needs no opt-in.
_comment_auth: Langfuse authenticates OTLP with HTTP Basic: base64(publicKey:secretKey) from a project's API keys page. Built at runtime from LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY / LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY in .env — never written here, because this file is tracked.
_comment_exporters: Traces are what build the phase/agent tree. Metrics and logs are cheap and land on the same endpoint, but Langfuse only consumes traces — set them to 'none' unless you are also pointing at a general OTLP collector.
_comment_toolDetails: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 puts tool names, subagent names and subagent_type on spans. This is what makes 'which agents were called / ran' answerable, so it is on. It logs tool METADATA, not prompt text.
_comment_privacy: PRIVACY — both OFF on purpose. OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS puts full prompt text (for Oneshot: ticket bodies, MR diffs, whatever the phase read out of the repo) into span payloads; OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES does the same for everything the model wrote. Turning either on makes the span store a second, unredacted copy of every conversation, rendered in a browser. The per-phase JSONL under state/runs/<iid>/ is ALREADY the system of record for conversation content and Langfuse links to it. Flip one only for a short, deliberate debugging session, then flip it back.
_comment_flush: Phase sessions are SHORT (a Haiku recall can be under 30s) and each is a separate CLI process, so the OTel default 60s interval would let a whole phase exit before its first export. Lowered so a finished phase is visible almost immediately. Set any to 0 to omit the variable and take the SDK default.
_comment_sessionAttribute: Langfuse groups traces into a session by the 'langfuse.session.id' attribute. Oneshot stamps it with the run id, so every phase of one ticket lands in one session view. UNVERIFIED against a live Langfuse: whether resource-level attributes propagate to spans for session grouping, or whether Langfuse requires it span-level, needs one real run to confirm — see docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.
_comment_resourceAttributes: Extra static key=value pairs merged into OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES on every span, on top of the per-spawn identity (oneshot.run_id, oneshot.ticket, oneshot.phase, oneshot.lap, oneshot.tier, langfuse.session.id) that src/lib/otel.ts adds. Values are percent-encoded before joining, so a comma or equals sign in one cannot break the variable.
